evidence: One cluster holds 1439 of the report's 4377 code units (33 percent) in 1162 sections across two generated files: module/deepmerge-ts.fuzz/src/type-soundness.generated.ts (1000 units) and src/declared-type-soundness.generated.ts (439 units). The section histogram is 1059 single-unit sections, 68 with two units, 13 with three and a tail up to eleven, so most sections are one generated case that happens to repeat a shape. Sampled bodies confirm the generator's fixed template: `{ const merged = deepmerge(null); const value = null; const check: typeof merged = value; return { merged, value: check, }; }` and `{ const merged = deepmerge(new Date(5), new Map<never, never>()); const check: typeof merged = new Map<never, never>(); return { merged, value: check, }; }`. Each case is a distinct type combination, which is the corpus's purpose; the file names already carry the .generated.ts suffix the repository uses for generated source.
action: Propose dismissal for the cluster, and record two structural points for the maintainer. First, a generated corpus of this size dominates the report: one third of all indexed units come from two files that no reviewer can act on, which dilutes every score band. Second, hash-based dismissal does not hold here, because regenerating the corpus changes bodies and paths and therefore the hash, so the same cluster re-surfaces after every regeneration. The repository already names generated files *.generated.ts, so the durable options are to recognise that suffix in the review workflow (the same mechanism proposed for the file-enforcer header in issue #612) or to have the generator emit each case with enough structural variety that the corpus stops clustering with itself. Excluding the files from the index is not proposed here, since the maintainer has ruled out new exclusion patterns for generated trees.

evidence: In rust-module/rust-linter-core/src/diagnostic.rs, line() at 204-206 and end_line() at 218-220 have character-identical bodies: self.labels.first().map_or(1, |label| label.span.line). end_line's doc comment promises 'the primary label's span end line, for renderers that report ranges', so it silently reports the start line. Verified the cause: pub struct Span in src/span.rs:17 carries only offset, length, line and column, so no end line is derivable without the source text; end_column() at 223-228 returns column + length, which is also wrong for any span crossing a newline because length is a byte count. Verified impact: rg over package/ for end_line and end_column finds no caller of either accessor, only these definitions, so the API is currently unused and unexercised by tests.
action: This is a correctness finding, not a deduplication one. Three competing actions for the issue: (a) delete both unused accessors, since a published crate should not expose a range API that cannot be computed from Span; (b) extend Span (or the label) with a computed end line and end column filled in where the span is built, which span_at_offset in src/context.rs already has the information for, then keep the accessors; (c) keep them and document that end_line equals line because Span carries no end line, which leaves renderers unable to report multi-line ranges. Whichever is chosen, end_column's byte-length-as-column-delta bug must be addressed in the same change, and a test must cover a span crossing a newline.

evidence: Two literal-set guards in pi-plugin/auto-mode/src/types.ts: isUndefinedOrReusableVerdictSource (240-248) accepts undefined, 'approve' and 'user-approve'; isVerdictValue (262-274) accepts 'approve', 'deny', 'ask', 'user-approve' and 'user-deny' and is the type predicate for VerdictData['verdict']. evidence: trySpawn (module/p-map-fork/src/p-map-iterable.ts:239-370) and pullNext (src/p-map.ts:315-475) are the two concurrency engines of the fork's two public entry points.
